The harvest covers 78 headings from [Conrad](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/finite-abelian.pdf), [Elman](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~rse/algebra_book.pdf), [Torres](https://web.ma.utexas.edu/users/gdavtor/notes/comb_group_theory.pdf), and [Neumann](https://mathweb.tifr.res.in/Documents/Publications/Lectures/tifr21.pdf): 73 incorporated, two already published, and three declined. The challenge-prone declines are Elman’s infinite bounded-exponent splitting theorem and Torres’s torus-knot classification; both require a genuinely different subject scope. Conrad’s nonabelian \(p\)-group remark is the remaining decline.

I opened both required published pages—including the rewritten free-groups page—and all 54 external dependency items at their operative sections. Confidence routes were nine published certifications, eleven judge-plus-audit records, and 34 dated audits, each supplemented by direct inspection. The complete dependency-by-dependency ledger is in [notes §8](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/frontier-10-batch-2.notes.md:181).

Convention decisions include \(G(p)\) for primary components, increasing invariant factors without unit factors, generic pushouts for arbitrary maps versus \(G*_K H\) only for monomorphisms, and an inverse-corrected Schreier action matching the library’s composition order. Torres’s unfinished normal-form proof is backed by Neumann’s construction. No published falsehood, forward reference, cross-batch dependency, external fallback, or applied-\(\iota\) violation was found.
